items.headline: Schedule more easily across time zones with time zone abbreviations in Google Calendar on the web
items.summary: Building on our recent launch allowing you to view up to three time zones in Google Calendar on the web , we’re making cross-time-zone scheduling even clearer by replacing raw GMT+/- offsets (such as GMT-5 or GMT-8) with familiar, locale-aware time zone abbreviations (such as ET, CT, MT, or PT for users in the United States or MEZ in Germany). Previously, unless you manually entered a custom label in Calendar Settings, time zone columns on your calendar grid and guest local times in “Find a time” only showed numeric GMT offsets. Whether you’re an executive assistant coordinating global leadership schedules or a team member booking meetings across regions, you’ll now see recognizable time zon
lines: Google Calendar on the web now shows locale-aware time zone abbreviations, such as ET, CT, MT, or PT for U.S. users and MEZ for users in Germany, instead of GMT offsets.
Previously, time zone columns and guest local times in Find a time showed only numeric GMT offsets unless a custom label was entered in Calendar Settings.
This helps users scheduling meetings across regions read time zones more easily.

items.headline: Simplifying multicloud networking to Azure with partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect
items.summary: As AI changes how businesses build and run applications, more enterprises are spreading their models, data and applications across multiple clouds. To make that work, they need fast, private connections between those environments. Historically, connecting multiple clouds has meant ordering physical connections from each provider, setting up networking on both sides, and coordinating across multiple teams. That process could take weeks or even months. We wanted to make that much simpler. Today, we're extending partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect to Microsoft Azure, now available in preview. The service is jointly supported by Google Cloud and Microsoft, and gives you a private, high-bandwidth co
lines: Google Cloud extended partner Cross-Cloud Interconnect to Microsoft Azure, now available in preview.
The service is jointly supported by Google Cloud and Microsoft and provides a private, high-bandwidth connection between the clouds.
Historically, connecting multiple clouds required ordering physical connections from each provider, which could take weeks or months.

items.headline: Researchers hijack Hugging Face account for popular Kokoro AI model
items.summary: A Lack of ownership verification on the Hugging Face platform allowed researchers to take control of Kokoro, a text-to-speech model used in projects from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Amazon Web Services. [...]
lines: Reported by BleepingComputer: Researchers took control of the Hugging Face account for Kokoro, a text-to-speech AI model.
Kokoro is used in projects from Google, NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, and Amazon Web Services, and the takeover was enabled by a lack of ownership verification on the Hugging Face platform.
Relevant for IT teams that depend on models hosted on Hugging Face, since account ownership verification was the gap.

items.headline: Oracle to Patch 11 Java Flaws Today as Critical OpenJDK RCE (CVE-2026-114938) Report Emerges
items.summary: Oracle is preparing to release security patches for 11 vulnerabilities in Java SE on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, all of which may be exploited remotely without authentication, as separate reports warn of a potentially critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw affecting OpenJDK. The 11 vulnerabilities carry a maximum CVSS 3.1 severity score of 8.1, according to Oracle's advance security notice.
lines: Oracle is preparing to release security patches for 11 vulnerabilities in Java SE on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, all of which may be exploited remotely without authentication, as separate reports warn of a potentially critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw affecting OpenJDK.
Reported by The Hacker News; not yet confirmed on an official page.
